title: Q3→Q4 Transition Communique & Ops Pulse
summary: Leadership reviewed Q3 performance vs plan, introduced a cautious hiring posture for Q4 to protect runway, walked through a prioritized Q4 roadmap focusing on reliability, cost optimizations, and private deployment features, and shared a brief incident postmortem. Action items assigned for capacity planning, security documentation, and a follow-up customer showcase.
action_items: Samir Gupta: deliver capacity plan & cost forecast by 2026-11-10
Priya Nair: circulate prioritized Q4 feature tracker and dependencies by 2026-11-05
Marcus Liao: finalize incident RCA and distro note by 2026-11-04
Elena Ortiz: update hiring freeze policy FAQ and manager comms by 2026-11-06
next_steps: Schedule ops deep-dive with Platform and Reliability (calendar invite)
Seq of customer showcases for enterprise pipeline (sales to coordinate)
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-11-02 10:00 PST | Duration: ~68 minutes | Attendees: Alicia Park, Marcus Liao, Priya Nair, Samir Gupta, Elena Ortiz, Derek Wu + all staff. Recording: yes. Deck: https://redwood.internal/q4-ops-deck (internal link)

00:00 Alicia Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna start on time, appreciate it. Uh quick housekeeping, we'll do updates, a short Q&A and then breakout rooms for team-level follow-ups. I'll kick off with the Q3 readout.
00:22 Alicia Park: So Q3 overall, net/net we came in slightly positive on revenue, ARR growth was 12% quarter-over-quarter, which is — uh — slightly under plan but ahead of last year. Our unit economics improvements via batching and caching helped offset model infra cost upticks. There's still work to do on churn in a couple of mid-market accounts.
01:05 Derek Wu: Quick question on churn — is that concentrated in any particular vertical? I know we lost a small fintech customer last month.
01:15 Alicia Park: Good call out. It's mostly two things: one, pricing/usage misalignment with mid-market and two, SSO integration friction in a few accounts. Sales is following up. Derek, you're on that.
01:30 Marcus Liao: I'll add that the infra side saw a 7% latency regression on the hosted fleet during peak windows in Sept, caused by a mismatch in batch sizing heuristics after a rollout. That triggered some throttling and fallback which increased cost. We rolled back the change and are tuning default batching policies.
01:55 Samir Gupta: The rollout gap was a config parity issue between canary and prod, so we're adding a gating test in CI to avoid misconfigured batch windows. Also, we're going to expose the "batching inspector" in Console as an experimental feature so teams can see live batch sizes and hit rates.
02:26 Priya Nair: On product, we shipped the embeddings endpoint improvements which dropped per-embedding GPU time by ~18% — nice work. For Q4, we're prioritizing three pillars: reliability (SRs), cost efficiency (batching/quantization), and private deployment features (VPC + on-prem packaging). Those are in the deck.
03:05 Alicia Park: I want to talk about hiring and budget. We've decided on a calibrated approach: a hiring posture adjustment across non-customer-facing roles. This is not a blanket freeze, but a prioritization; customer-critical hires and revenue-generating roles continue. We'll post details to the handbook.
03:30 Elena Ortiz: We'll send managers a template for hiring justification and an FAQ. Immediate question — what about contractors? We'll handle case-by-case but leaning toward preserving critical external support for platform ops.
03:50 Audience Q (Speaker 1): Are there changes to compensation or benefits?
03:55 Alicia Park: No changes to comp/benefits. This is about headcount cadence to ensure runway while we hit Q4 milestones.
04:10 Marcus Liao: Quick infra highlight: we had a Sev 2 incident mid-October where a memory leak in a new kernel path caused slow recoveries on dedicated clusters. Root cause is a socket leak in a vendor kernel op; we've patched the runtime and mitigations are in place. Full RCA is coming.
04:35 Samir Gupta: To be explicit — customer impact was limited to a handful of Dedicated tenants that were on a mix of older drivers; hosted customers had graceful fallback to smaller model variants. We're adding driver compatibility checks to our pre-deploy verification.
05:05 Priya Nair: On the private deployment roadmap, key ask from enterprise pilots: automated key rotation via KMS/HSM integration, longer retention for audit logs, and simplified on-prem packaging. We're scoping an alpha for a pilot partner in January.
05:40 Derek Wu: Sales note: we have three late-stage deals for Dedicated with compliance-heavy buyers. The security upgrades — KMS, audit logs, SOC 2 attestations — will materially affect conversion; pushing for those in Q4.
06:10 Alicia Park: On metrics culture — we're simplifying the OKR dashboard. Expect a trimmed view to surface leading indicators: latency P95, cost per 1K tokens, canary failure rate, and renewal risk score.
06:30 Audience Q (Speaker 2): Will product roadmaps change because of the hiring posture?
06:38 Priya Nair: Prioritization is tighter. We're trimming low-adoption features and focusing resources on the pillars I mentioned. We will, however, keep R&D on a couple experimental efforts but on smaller teams.
07:05 Marcus Liao: A note on cost optimization: quantization profiles are working well on a subset of models, but we saw quality regressions on long-context prompts. So we'll keep quantization for retrieval & short generation workloads, and run more evals for long-context to understand QoL tradeoffs.
07:40 Alicia Park: We also want to keep the momentum on customer success and transparency. We'll surface more per-account performance analytics to customers so they can tune prompts and routing.
08:05 Priya Nair: Quick product demo — I'm going to screen-share (transcript note: demo referred to deck slide 12). The new route config UI shows fallback policies (latency-first, cost-first), model pinning per route, and rollout control. It's lightweight but it maps to canary + auto-fallback.
08:40 [Demo noise, indistinct chatter]
09:10 Priya Nair: Sorry audio — in the demo you can see a route pinned to 'redwood-m3-small' and a fallback to a quantized variant. We show expected delta in latency and cost per 1K tokens.
09:38 Audience Q (Speaker 3): Is there a way to get A/B rollout metrics per route?
09:44 Priya Nair: Yes, in Console under 'Rollouts' you'll get traffic split, model-level metrics, and error budget burn. We're adding per-prompt quality tracking as well.
10:05 Marcus Liao: Infrastructure ask: teams need more visibility into per-request KV cache hit rates — we plan to surface that in tracing and the Console. There was one case where poor cache keying caused low hit rates and increased token cost.
10:40 Samir Gupta: Ops note — we're adding quotas at a model-level to prevent noisy tenants from saturating pool. It's an admin-level control in the Console. We'll also add alerts for abnormal batch size distributions.
11:05 Elena Ortiz: People ops update — new parental leave policy finalizing next week; we'll announce details. Also, mental health benefit expansion pilot starting Q1.
11:30 Audience Q (Speaker 4): Can we get more transparency on hiring decisions?
11:35 Alicia Park: Yes, we'll publish the criteria and the prioritized hiring pipeline. Managers will get a weekly digest on open reqs and stats.
11:50 Marcus Liao: Back to incidents — there's also an open reliability initiative to reduce cold-start latency by improving KV cache warm-up and pre-warming inference workers. Expected impact is a ~30% reduction in tail latencies for cold requests.
12:15 Priya Nair: Product roadmap highlight: GA of 'Private Connect' for VPC peering and a simplified on-prem installer. Also GA of structured output enforcement for function-calling in Q4 Beta.
12:40 Derek Wu: Sales highlight — three logo expansions in enterprise space, plus a renewed commitment from a major marketplace partner. We should prepare case studies for Q1.
13:05 Audience Q (Speaker 5): Are we going to open an APAC office?
13:10 Alicia Park: APAC expansion is still a go but on a measured timeline; cloud region partnerships will be primary. People office in APAC not immediate but under review.
13:30 [crosstalk, laughter]
13:50 Priya Nair: OK, OKR updates: we're re-baselining a few stretch metrics given current pace, but maintaining ambition. We'll publish the updated OKR doc later today.
14:10 Marcus Liao: Security update: SOC 2 Type II audit is in progress, and our compliance team is prepping evidence. We're also rolling out SAML improvements and tightened RBAC defaults.
14:40 Samir Gupta: Any questions about private release scheduling? We're targeting a small pilot in Jan, bigger beta in March.
15:00 Audience Q (Speaker 6): How are we measuring model quality across releases?
15:05 Priya Nair: We're building a quality dashboard tied to eval suites per workload; we run regression checks on canary and track user-facing metrics like completion correctness and hallucination rate for retrieval tasks.
15:30 Alicia Park: Final thoughts — focus on finishing strong in Q4. Small teams with tight scopes will make it possible. Transparency and alignment are critical. We'll host a deeper ops forum next Tuesday — invite will go out.
15:55 Elena Ortiz: Thank you everyone. We'll post an FAQ and the recording.
16:05 Breakout rooms: team-specific sessions (not transcribed here)

Note: transcription contains typical Fireflies artifacts: occasional misheard proper nouns, dropped punctuation, and speaker attribution inconsistencies. For security docs and deck links see internal share in Slack #all-hands and the Q4-ops-deck link above.
